Shows advisory playback-health banners and recovery notices during playback. Automatic recovery still runs silently when off, and fatal errors are always shown.
Disables certificate verification for newly started desktop mpv playback. Enable this only for a server you trust: an attacker could intercept your connection.

Used for the initial request whenever a VLC player is active. In-player quality choices last only until playback ends. High-bitrate playback through VLC can crash the app or the device, so a conservative default is preset.
Finite limits may ask the server to transcode. Maximum bitrate separately controls bandwidth for remote servers.

Standard asks the server for a compatible stream above JellyScope's input envelope (4K30 on iOS; 4K60-equivalent for LibVLC on macOS). Unrestricted lets the active player try the original source, but may cause stutter, frozen video, or playback failure.

Collection is off by default. Sanitized logs stay on this device until you send them to your Jellyfin server. Turning collection off deletes stored logs. Desktop collection also includes playback probes.
Couldn’t update diagnostic log collection. Try again.
Show playback info at start opens the playback info overlay automatically when playback begins; it stays toggleable from the player controls.
Writes UNSANITIZED logs to the system log. Use only while reproducing a bug on a release build.

Every upload includes a diagnostic snapshot with your app version, device model, and OS. When available, the snapshot also includes this device’s decoder capabilities and technical details from the most recent playback failure (codec, resolution, and frame rate — never titles or file paths). Turning off Collect diagnostic logs removes only captured app log lines; the diagnostic snapshot is still included.
Client log upload is disabled on this Jellyfin server. A server administrator must enable Dashboard → Advanced → “Allow client log upload” (EnableClientLogUpload) before diagnostics can be sent.
